clause_that_reaches_it: Where the same product question is answered in more than one place, it has one answer. A second surface or a second code path may not answer it differently.
why_in_scope: The question is 'what is at this catalog record's outputPath, and does it match what was compiled for it?' Two things answer it: the Publication row in PublicationStore's catalog (which names an outputPath and, by existing at all, claims that path IS that edition) and the actual bytes on disk at that path. Before the P1 fix, Republisher.republish staged its output under a filename built from snap.config's nextVersion, which was pinned to the ORIGINAL edition's version — so the staged file, once moved into Exports/, silently landed at the SAME path as the record it was republished from: the catalog kept naming the original record at that path while the bytes underneath it were now the new edition's. One question, two disagreeing answers, and nothing told the writer or Claude which was true. The mint-first fix makes every compile/republish mint its version — and therefore its filename — before compiling. 'Distinct by construction' is the whole-branch review's correction to that sentence and is now earned rather than asserted: the minted republish version is CHECKED against the catalog and re-drawn while taken (Republisher.uniqueRepublishVersion), because the four-character suffix is a 65,536-value pool every republish of one edition draws from — and if anything is nevertheless already at the destination path, the job fails loudly and leaves those bytes alone instead of deleting them. So every catalog record's outputPath is distinct, an existing record's bytes can never be touched by a later compile, and the catalog and the filesystem can no longer disagree.
intent_expressed_when: not at all — a republish request expresses intent to create a NEW edition, never to overwrite the one already sitting in Exports/
call_path: MCP `republish` (RepublishTool, Maugham/MCP/Tools/PublicationTools.swift) -> Republisher.republish(snapshotID:format:label:) -> mint the version -> PDFCompiler/EPUBCompiler render into a filename carrying that version -> move staged output into Exports/ -> PublicationStore.append. CompileOrchestrator.compile shares the same mint-then-render ordering for the initial compile.

reason: the unconditional EMISSION.md refresh is a deliberate app-owned-doc policy (F5): the file is generated, carries no writer content, and refreshing it on refused compiles is the point — an agent reading it must never meet a stale copy.
